newsitem.title: USA: U.S. drops charges against ex-KGB agent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drops charges against ex-KGB agent.

text.p: The United States dismissed espionage charges on Thursday against a former KGB agent accused of trying to steal secrets of the Star Wars defence programme.

Vladimir Galkin, dressed in prison khakis, smiled slightly as the charges against him were dismissed. The 50-year-old former spy, who was arrested in New York last month, was accused of trying to obtain secret information from a Northborough, Massachusetts employee of Data General Corp. on the Star Wars programme in 1991.

"It was a mistake," Galkin said of his arrest after a 15-minute hearing in the U.S. Distict Court in Worcester, about an hour's drive west of Boston. "I don't know who is responsble for this mistake."

Russians "reacted strongly to the arrest. They protested strongly and demanded his release and made clear they would retaliate," a U.S. intelligence official said. "It was concluded that on balance the charges should be dismissed in the national interest."
The formal written motion to dismiss submitted to U.S. Magistrate Charles Swartwood included the phrase "in the national interest."
The ex-spy, who spoke by telephone to his wife and daughter during the news conference, told reporters, "In my case, I was a private person coming here and they could arrest a private person.
"I did not accept their position. The United States against Galkin. It was the United States against Russia," he said, adding that "this is the first occasion for them to arrest a former spy."
He said he planned to return to Russia in the next day or two.
Earlier in Washington the Justice Department issued a statement announcing the dismissal and defending its actions.
"The CIA was advised, prior to Galkin's entry, of the proposed arrest. While concerns were raised, in the end no objections were interposed," the department said in a statement.

"In retrospect and after further consultations within the government, the CIA has concluded, and the State Department has concurred, that the national interest would best be served by dismissing the charges. The Department of Justice has accepted this recommendation and moved to dismiss the case," the statement said.
